original_test_intent: Verify end-to-end liquid-leak protection for the intended sensor cable: a controlled vendor-approved wetting or simulator stimulus must assert the mapped BMC leak event and produce the documented host/system power response without harming energized hardware, then recover to a known dry/normal state.
original_method: Select the unique row; identify SUT/BMC, leak cable/sensor zone/channel and adjacent electrical/liquid-cooling hardware; obtain the vendor fixture/test-fluid and safety procedure; drain workloads, establish console and emergency power isolation, document baseline dry sensor, SEL and host power; contain the zone and apply the exact bounded stimulus by a qualified operator; record sensor assertion, SEL payload/timing and host/power transition; remove/dry/reset only as documented; verify deassertion, final power/health and absence of damage; never improvise ordinary water or repeat automatically.
manual_activity: A qualified hardware operator establishes containment and power safety, applies only the vendor-approved leak simulator/fluid to the exact sensor zone, observes physical response and dries/restores the system; the agent may collect read-only post-stimulus telemetry.
required_inputs: SUT/BMC/firmware and physical leak cable/sensor zone/channel/location map
Vendor-approved simulator, conductive test pad or test fluid with exact quantity/contact/dwell/removal procedure
Expected sensor state plus SEL sensor/type/severity/assert/deassert payload and timing
Expected host/chassis/pump/valve/power action, hard aborts, containment/PPE/ESD/electrical isolation, dry-out and final-state recovery
safety_requirements: Never drop ordinary water onto or near energized electronics by improvisation
Use a dedicated quiesced SUT, qualified operator, containment and immediate independent power isolation
Photograph/map the exact sensor target and keep stimulus within the approved amount/zone
Preserve SEL and power evidence without clearing logs; stop on escape, short, odor, heat, unexpected shutdown or hardware fault
Do not re-energize or repeat until dryness and hardware safety are independently confirmed
agent_execution_scope: Before stimulus, collect read-only BMC/SEL/chassis/host baseline and verify target mapping
After operator action, timestamp and collect sensor/SEL/power/host evidence and deassertion/final-state telemetry
Correlate observed event with the approved sensor and power-response oracle
Do not apply liquid, control unsafe power, clear SEL, declare dryness, authorize repeat/re-energization or decide verdict
engineer_actions: Approve exact sensor/cable zone and safe non-damaging stimulus/fixture
Approve SEL and physical/power response including timing, thresholds and aborts
Approve containment, isolation, dry-out/deassertion, final state and damage/recovery ownership
Review physical and telemetry evidence and decide PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Post-stimulus `ipmitool sel list` and chassis status are useful read-only evidence, but they cannot perform or validate the physical stimulus and a filtered log alone may hide severity/context.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Qualified operator uses the approved fixture/fluid; collect complete timestamped SEL, mapped sensor reading, chassis power/status and host/console evidence before/asserted/deasserted states without clearing logs.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Booted OS, physical leak-cable stimulus, system power check, SEL/system criteria and 10/10-minute estimate remain; unsafe ordinary-water improvisation is prohibited.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Treat stimulus safety, sensor assertion, BMC event, protective power response and dry-state recovery as five independently evidenced checkpoints tied to one physical sensor zone.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds exact topology, vendor fixture/fluid bounds, containment/electrical safety, decoded event/timing, expected protective action, deassertion and hardware recovery.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A generic SEL line does not prove the intended cable sensed the stimulus or that the required power protection occurred; a shutdown alone could be an unsafe short rather than correct leak logic.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Real liquid can bridge circuitry, corrode connectors or enter cooling/electrical assemblies; even a correct protective shutdown does not establish that hardware is safe to re-energize.

project_override_considerations: A vendor electrical leak-sensor simulator is preferred when it exercises the same controller input and protection path; if it bypasses the physical cable/wetting element, engineering must state whether that loses required coverage. Any real-fluid method must be explicitly approved for this platform and location.
expected_evidence: Pre-stimulus dry sensor, complete SEL and host/chassis/power baseline
Stimulus timestamp plus sensor assertion and decoded SEL payload/timing
Expected versus observed host/pump/valve/chassis power transition and independent console timeline
Removal/dryness, sensor deassertion, final power/health, damage inspection and recovery record

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Procedure and Criteria consistently require a physical leak stimulus followed by BMC SEL and system/power status checks. Safety and exact expected reactions are missing but not contradictory.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The physical leak-protection purpose is identifiable and a vendor-approved safe simulator/fluid procedure can make it executable. MANUAL ONLY reflects the required operator action; unsafe improvised water remains a stop condition for execution.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Functionality row 2246 Wistron-BMC Sanity-00028-V001: approve the SUT/BMC and exact leak cable/sensor zone/channel map; vendor-approved simulator/test fluid, quantity/contact/dwell/removal and whether it preserves physical coverage; expected sensor state, SEL sensor/type/severity/assert/deassert payload/timing and host/pump/valve/chassis power response; containment, PPE/ESD/electrical isolation, hard aborts, dry-out/re-energization criteria, final state and damage/recovery ownership.

review_improvement: Preserves the real leak-sensor and protection-path coverage while replacing an unsafe informal water step with a controlled, traceable and recoverable hardware procedure.
independent_technical_reasoning: A leak test is not validated merely by producing an SEL entry: the correct physical sensor must assert, the event must map to it, the documented protective power behavior must follow, and the sensor must safely recover after removal. Ordinary water near live electronics can itself cause the shutdown or damage that the protection logic is meant to prevent, making such an outcome uninterpretable and dangerous. The stimulus and dryness judgment are inherently physical, while telemetry collection can only assist after a qualified operator controls the setup.
